items.title: "The Shot I Almost Had" (small buffalo calf) — Option 1A approved
items.subtitle: Francois approved Option 1A (firelight cover). Posting Friday 25 Sept. Option 1B banked for a future post.
items.ask:
Timing: Holding this for tomorrow (Fri 25 Sept), not today — today's feed is wall-to-wall Heritage Day/Braai Day content, and organic posts tend to get buried in that noise. Posting the day after clears the clutter.

Cover: The Shot I Almost Had

Option 1A — firelight: Keeps the campfire visual thread running (the 'told at a fire, not a slide' identity) — moodier, intimate, night-time read.
Option 1B — green bushveld, daylight: Closer to the literal moment as you told it — calf alone on a gravel road in daylight. More grounded, less staged.
Both keep your exact story beats and your own line, word for word — nothing paraphrased into coach-speak.

Caption: I had a small buffalo calf lined up — alone on a gravel road, completely still. I wanted a better angle. Moved the car a few metres. By the time I looked back up, it was gone. Just an empty road where the shot used to be.

I didn't miss it because I was too slow. I missed it because I was waiting for perfect.

That's the trap for a lot of business owners too — holding back the imperfect version because the perfect one is still one adjustment away. It never comes. The opportunity does, once, and then it's back in the bush.

Don't wait to be perfect in your imperfection.

What's the shot you've been waiting to line up perfectly, instead of just taking?

#BushLessons #NewWaysOfSeeing #Leadership #ExecutiveCoaching

Reply 1A or 1B, or APPROVED for your favorite as-is.

Also: we're coming up on a month working together — would love to grab 20-30 min on Zoom next week for an update and progress check. Let us know a time that works.

items.title: "What I Didn't See Coming" (water monitor / crocodile) — Option 2A approved
items.subtitle: Francois approved Option 2A (starlit fire cover). Posting Friday 25 Sept. Option 2B banked for a future post.
items.ask:
Timing: Same as Option 1 — holding for tomorrow (Fri 25 Sept) rather than posting into today's Heritage Day noise.

Cover: What I Didn't See Coming

Option 2A — starlit fire: Same campfire-storytelling thread as 1A, tenser and moodier — fits the 'zoomed in, then it exploded' beat.
Option 2B — green bushveld road, daylight: A calmer, literal establishing shot of the riverbank setting — lets the caption carry the tension instead of the image.
This is genuinely new material (no earlier post covers this one) and it's self-contained — good one to bank cleanly either way.

Caption: I was in a hide on a riverbank, camera zoomed right in on a water monitor moving toward a crocodile's nest. I had the shot lined up, patient, waiting.

Then the whole scene exploded. The monitor bolted at full speed.

What I hadn't seen — because it was outside my frame — was the crocodile, already moving to protect its eggs.

Most business owners live zoomed in. Day-to-day, task to task, deal to deal. That's necessary. But it isn't enough on its own — you also need to zoom out. Scan the wider landscape. Notice what's shifting before it's already on top of you.

Whatever's coming for your business rarely announces itself inside the frame you're already watching.

Where in your business are you zoomed in, when you need to be zoomed out?

#BushLessons #NewWaysOfSeeing #Leadership #ExecutiveCoaching

Reply 2A or 2B, or APPROVED for your favorite as-is.
